rows.title: CT will keep programs hurt by federal shutdown afloat — for now
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont said it’s premature to commit any of last year’s $2.5 billion surplus to plug holes in federal funding over the long term.

rows.title: Audit: Lamont staff fumbled vehicle oversight, had laptop surplus
rows.standfirst: The governor’s office did not maintain proper oversight of state vehicles and kept three computers for every staff member, auditors found.

rows.title: Why are CT Medicaid costs rising? GOP wants auditors to find out
rows.standfirst: The GOP caucus asked the state auditors ‘to reveal potential efficiency measures which could produce significant savings for taxpayers.’

rows.title: CT finalizing plan to blunt funding cuts amid government shutdown
rows.standfirst: CT legislators are planning a Nov. 12-13 special session to OK using up to $500 million to blunt federal cutbacks to human service programs.

rows.title: CT House GOP pitches $700-per-filer middle class income tax cut
rows.standfirst: Instead of spending $500 million to offset federal cuts, CT’s GOP leaders asked, why not use the money to cut state income tax burdens?

rows.title: SNAP benefits poised to stop Nov. 1 despite CT hopes to continue
rows.standfirst: If SNAP funding dries up next month as threatened, that will put increasing pressure on Connecticut food pantries to fill the need.

rows.title: CT officials ask: Could tax cuts and credits counter federal aid loss?
rows.standfirst: There are no legal obstacles blocking CT government from cutting taxes, but the political challenges remain plentiful.

rows.title: CT will bolster heat assistance program as federal funds stall
rows.standfirst: Replacing LIHEAP funds with state money will cost Connecticut millions monthly, though the state can seek federal reimbursement after the shutdown.

rows.title: CT lawmakers: Lamont must do more to replace vanishing food aid
rows.standfirst: A bipartisan consensus is nudging Gov. Ned Lamont toward tapping Connecticut’s rainy day fund to replace SNAP benefits.

rows.title: Trump ordered to pay SNAP benefits; CT officials still want to help
rows.standfirst: The rulings didn’t stop CT state legislators’ demands to reserve hundreds of millions to shore up SNAP and other human service programs.
